Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ogis 2026.11.26.3

  • Documentation only. og_tracks()’ help, its error for compare, a test’s name and the tracks article call its second set of column names upper-case ones (VESSEL_ID, DATE_TIME, …), and the compare example’s second source other; the older entries here are worded alike. Text only: nothing behaves differently but the error’s wording.

ogis 2026.11.26.2

  • og_cells(pixel = FALSE): the fixed sizes alone, opening on the finest. The user (2026-11-26), on an effort map of 0.001-degree cells: “there is no difference between grid - about a pixel, fine (heavy), coarser and 0.001 degrees. suggest we just”start” at 0.001”. Where the cells’ own size is about a pixel at the zooms they are looked at, the three choices draw the finest size; with pixel = FALSE Cells lists the sizes (and H3’s) alone. pixel = TRUE, as before, by default.
  • A bundle carries every size offered. Its levels started at 0.01 degrees, so a size offered under it (0.005, 0.001) found no level and a bundle drew another size for it; the effort map had passed the finer levels to og_bundle(grids = ) by hand.

ogis 2026.11.26.1

  • A grid cell with no value is grey, said so in the legend (“no value”, shown while such a cell is in view) and in its popup. Before, a cell whose every row lacked the value shown was drawn in the palette’s lowest colour, as a small value: the page read a missing value as 0, and a bundle wrote it as 0. The user (2026-11-26), on an effort map where 13,441 of 148,237 cells hold hauls with no soak: “fix the no-soak colour in ogis - think we should user a grey colour for NA”. A bundle now writes a missing sum as missing and sums only the values a cell’s rows have, as DuckDB’s sum() does on a served map; a coarser cell with some values is coloured by them.

ogis 2026.11.26

  • og_cells() draws H3’s hexagons beside the squares: where the cells carry an H3 index (a column h3, or the one named by h3 =), the page’s Cells offers hexagons at a resolution following the zoom (an edge of four pixels or more, a hexagon about eight across) or at one resolution at every zoom, from the cells’ own to seven coarser, in the same list as the squares, the c-square and the ICES rectangle. DuckDB sums the cells to the H3 cell that holds them at the resolution drawn (h3_cell_to_parent()), and a value is per km² of each hexagon’s own area. A table may carry both grids on each row (a row for each square and hexagon that meet), or H3 alone (cell = "h3" or "h3_9" opens on them). The user (2026-11-26), for effort maps: “We could both think of this as a grid level or hex (h3) level … the C-square is just one dimension.” H3 had been set aside for fishycode’s effort map on speed (decision 220: 0.7-1.1 s a tile on 524 M cells); on another effort map (148,237 cells at 0.001 degrees and H3 resolution 11, served from its Parquet file) a whole view at zoom 10 redraws in 0.25-1.0 s on every grid, H3 resolution 11’s 63,460 hexagons in view included (measured in the page, 2026-11-26). H3 needs DuckDB’s community extension h3, installed on first use.
  • A bundle offers the squares alone, saying the hexagons are left out: its cells are summed by the browser, which knows squares only. Cells with no squares are left out of a bundle.

ogis 2026.11.22.5

  • The article A page of your own steps through a time panel’s window: two buttons of a page’s script set the window to a day and the next (og.window()), and the script’s box says which day is shown (og.on("window")), on a vessel of og_example("dansk") drawn by og_tracks(), its pings following the window, by speed, black the slowest. The tracks article says what the map now shows of the window, and that the pings are by speed.

ogis 2026.11.22.4

  • og_tracks() colours its pings by speed, in Inferno, black the slowest, and by what the vessel was doing as a choice in the page (Colour by), in the colours of the activity lane; before, by what it was doing alone, speed only where the pings had no activity, in viridis. The maintainer (2026-11-22), on a trip check: “the device speed should be the default colour of pings. And i am used to the inverse viridis when it comes to speed (black - low speed)”, then “I mean inferno”. Asked where in ogis: in og_tracks(), which knows its speed column; og_point() stays general, viridis for a number, and the time panel’s own points already ran Inferno from black. With the pings by speed, On top (2026.11.22.3) draws the slow or the fast ones over the others.
  • A palette by column, for a choice of colours: og_point(colour = c(behaviour, speed), palette = list(speed = "inferno")), each column its own palette, a column not named keeping its default, for every layer function with palette. One palette had served every column of the choice, so a number’s and a category’s could not both be chosen.

ogis 2026.11.22.3

  • Points coloured by a number have a switch, On top: the rows in their order, as before and by default, or low or high values on top. The maintainer (2026-11-22): “that the user can ‘arrange’ the pings in the plot so that e.g. the slowest come on top. This should be a switch in the app”, for every point layer coloured by a number (asked whether by default or by an argument). It is under the layer’s name in the page, applies at once, goes into the address as <id>_ontop, and holds over a change of base map; with a choice of colours (colour = c(behaviour, speed)) it orders by the colour shown, and a colour of categories orders nothing. It is MapLibre’s circle-sort-key, read from the layer’s state (og_layer(state = )): a point’s class along the colour’s scale, 32 classes four to each of the palette’s nine stops, whatever the stretch, the rows in their order within a class and a missing value under all. MapLibre draws each key of a tile at once, so a key for each value would be a draw call for each point. Measured in headless Chrome (Apple M4 Pro), a served map of 200,000 points as tiles, 166,000 in view: the switch re-lays the tiles, the map settled 0.22-0.25 s after it (0.13 s back to the rows’ order), and a frame took the same time in each. A sort key given in MapLibre’s terms (og_point("circle-sort-key" = )) replaces the switch.

ogis 2026.11.22.2

  • The panel’s other layers follow its window: og_time(follow = ), "window" by default. A layer that carries the group and a time (og_point(), og_segment(), og_path()) showed the group’s whole span, wherever the window was set, so a trip opened with a few pings either side, or a window dragged on the chart, showed more on the map than on the chart. A page built on the panel filtered its layers to the window itself (og.filter() on the features’ time, og_t). The maintainer (2026-11-22): “By default I wanted only the trip window proper to appear both in space and time”; asked whether ogis should do it by default, the window. Those layers now show the rows of the window alone (a path’s run where it overlaps the window, whole), and follow it each time it is set: a drag, a double click, a lane, og.window(). follow = "span" shows the span’s, as before. Each window the reader sets is one filter on each such layer, laid out again in MapLibre’s worker, where a span was filtered once. Measured in headless Chrome (Apple M4 Pro), a served map of one vessel’s 200,000 pings a minute as tiles: a window of a day set with og.window(), the map settled after a median 615 ms following the window and 582 ms following the span (five windows each, the camera’s move included), so the filter adds little to the move. og_tracks() takes the default.

ogis 2026.11.22.1

  • The time panel’s path lies under the map’s points, and its own points are optional: og_time(dots = ). The window’s path and points were drawn over every layer, so a point layer of the same rows (og_tracks()’ pings) lay under a white line and under the panel’s own points, in another colour. The maintainer (2026-11-22), on a trip check: “The white track line should not have a point. And the pings should be on top of the white track line”. The page there moved the panel’s layers by their ids and hid its points, again after each change of base map. The window’s path is now drawn under the lowest of the panel’s point and segment layers (og_point(), og_segment(): those with the group and a time), over its other layers (a path), and its points, rings and hover over every layer, as before; the order holds when a layer’s data come late and over a change of base map. dots = FALSE leaves out the panel’s own points, and with them the click that marks a row’s time on the chart; marked rows keep their rings. og_tracks() passes it, as its pings are the panel’s rows.

ogis 2026.11.22

  • A page’s script reads and sets the time panel’s window, and hears it change: og.window() and og.on("window", fn), documented in og_script(). A page built on the panel had to call the page’s internal tSetWindow(), judge the series loaded by its internal TS, and poll the address’s tw to follow the reader (a trip check built on ogis). og.window() gives the window shown, [from, to] in seconds on the panel’s clock, or null (no panel, a series loading, a span of no rows); og.window([from, to]) sets it as a drag across the chart does, and og.window(null) shows the whole span. Asked for before the series has loaded, the window is set once it has, in place of the address’s. og.on("window", fn) calls fn({window, group, span}) each time the window is drawn (a drag, a double click, a lane, another group or span, og.window()), and at once with the window shown, if there is one.

ogis 2026.11.21.2

  • A lane takes a layer’s colours whether the layer comes before the panel or after it. In 2026.11.21.1 a lane of a column the map colours by took the layer’s colours only when the layer was added before og_time(), so og_tracks(), which adds its pings after its panel (they then show the panel’s vessel and span alone), drew its activity lane in Paired and its pings in Okabe-Ito: “Fishing” light blue in the lane, sky blue on the map. The layer’s colours are now laid over the lanes each time the map is made, from the first layer that colours by the lane’s column; colours named in lane_palette still win.

ogis 2026.11.21.1

  • A lane’s value has one colour, solid, the same in every span: og_time(lane_palette = ). The lanes were coloured from Pastel 1, eight pale colours given to the values in the order they first came in the span shown, so “Fishing” could be one colour in one trip and another in the next, and the lanes read as washed out. The maintainer (2026-11-21), on a trip-check page: “Care to then not make the lower time panel so transparent. And use brewer pal 12”, and asked whether in ogis or in the page, “Change ogis”. Each interval’s colour is now set in R, by its value, over the lane’s values in every group and span: colours named by value in lane_palette (c(Fishing = "#ff7f00")) first; else, for a lane of a column a layer added before the panel colours by (og_point(), og_path()), that layer’s colour, so a value is one colour on the map and in the lane; else Brewer’s Paired, its twelve colours given to the values in their order (numbers as numbers: 9 before 10), over and over. A palette’s name or colours in lane_palette stand in for Paired. The bars are drawn solid, and a label inside one is written in white on a dark colour and dark on a light one, whichever has the more contrast. An interval with no label stays grey.

ogis 2026.11.21

  • The time panel draws every row on the map, unless told otherwise. The window’s path joined only every k-th ping and its points were thinned alike, to about 5,000 (the documentation said the path was drawn whole). Over a vessel’s whole series of 63,740 pings, “1 in 13 drawn on the map”, the path cut corners, and a point layer beside it showed pings with no line through them. The maintainer (2026-11-21): “plot everything unless explicitly told not to do so”; thinning “was only supposed to deal with the view”. The new og_time(thin = ) asks for it: FALSE by default, a number of rows (TRUE for 5,000) thins a window of more than that to about that many, a marked row always kept, and a window narrowed on the chart is thinned less, then not at all. The chart was not thinned, and is not: it is given every row, and uPlot’s line runs, in each column of pixels, from the least value of the rows there to the most, over the window shown, so a drag spreads them out again. og_tracks() takes the default, every row drawn.
  • What it costs, measured in headless Chrome (157, Apple M4 Pro): one vessel a ping a minute, the map settled after the window was set (the median of five; the camera’s move left out). The whole series of 60,000 pings: 250 ms, where the thinned window took 33 ms; of 500,000: 2.7 s, where it took 33 ms. Most of it is in MapLibre’s worker, the line’s data ready after 0.6 s, the points’ after 1.4 s and their 500,000 circles laid out by 2.6 s; the page itself is held once, for 0.6 s, as the window’s points are handed to the worker (0.06 s at 60,000). A window of 5,000 pings: 33 ms, as before. The chart: 1.4 ms at 60,000 rows and 11 ms at 500,000. thin keeps a long window quick.

ogis 2026.11.19.1

  • og_names() turns a name by its angle, a column of the names in degrees counter-clockwise from level, as og_text()’s angle (a missing angle level), the name turning with the map. A list of names lettered along their features (a trough, a long ground) no longer lies level. The column is how a name is drawn, not what a click shows. Asked by fishycode’s plan 078 (ask i), for MFRI’s place names carried by its internal package.

ogis 2026.11.19

  • A served map’s og_cells(filter = ) is tested in a browser, as a bundle’s was: the page opens with the choices given (a gear, a preset, a span of years) set in its controls from /meta’s options, draws those cells alone, and writes them into its address; a choice in the address wins. No change to the package. A fault was reported on fishycode’s plan 078 demo (bottom trawl, 2015-2024, on the 32-million-row Icelandic effort: “all”, no years, nothing drawn). It did not reproduce in headless Chrome or the app’s browser pane, on public data or the internal file, served alone or beside the other maps. The screenshots had been taken before the page’s first view: the page sets its controls only once /meta has come and the map has drawn its first frame, and a map of the depth alone was as blank at that moment. With the layer’s start ignored, the new test fails 6 of its 8 checks.

ogis 2026.11.18.17

  • A vessel whose id has a space has its effort’s cells in a served page. The page writes the tiles’ query as a form does (URLSearchParams), a space as +, and the server read the + as itself (utils::URLdecode()), so it refused every cells tile that named such a vessel (“the server refused tiles (HTTP 400): cells_vid is vessel 4, …”), and the map stayed empty of effort. The server now reads every query as a form writes it: + a space, %2B a plus, the bytes as UTF-8, a value split at its first = only; the tiles, the time panel’s series, a fit’s view and a map’s own routes alike (og_serve(routes = ): a + written in a route’s query is now a space; write %2B). A bundle was not touched: its page reads its own queries.
  • og_tracks(pings = x) with no map starts one, as og_tracks(x) does, where it stopped with “map is an og_map(); the pings go to pings”. Something else in the map’s place with pings given is still refused.

ogis 2026.11.18.16

  • Vessel tracks in one line, og_tracks() (ogis as a quick visual check of each step of a track’s processing, ramb doing the processing). Pings, as ramb leaves them (vid, time, lon, lat, speed, trip_id, gear, hours, behaviour) or with upper-case names (VESSEL_ID, DATE_TIME, …), become the track and its pings coloured by what the vessel did; a time panel of speed under the map, a vessel chosen there and then one of its trips, with lanes of activity, trips and any more given (another method’s trips, an observer’s labels) and marks (flags, planted faults); and the fishing effort by cell, summed from the fishing pings’ hours by vessel, gear and year, following the vessel chosen. On ramb’s dansk (395,000 pings, 14 vessels; ramb’s flags, harbours, jepol trips and hours in 4 s) the map built in 1.7 s. On about a million pings (10 vessels, served on this computer only), from the raw file through ramb to the map in 9 s. The map has no layer of each vessel’s whole path: such a path ran over every span’s ends and was drawn whole, a year’s tangle over the trip chosen; the panel draws the chosen span’s path itself. time_label names the clock ("as written (zone unknown)" where it is not known). A trip is ramb’s voyage_key where the pings have one (one key per trip across vessels and years, from ramb 2026.11.18, at this viewer’s wish), taken as it is; a vessel’s trip numbered from 1 is known by its vessel too. With ramb’s rb_flag_ping_clock_jump() the clock’s jumps are marks.
  • og_tracks(compare = ): where two columns disagree, two methods’ trips or an inferred activity against an observer’s: each a lane, and the panel marks, a row each, the pings one has and the other has not and, where the two share their values, those they give differently. On the million pings, two methods’ trips differ on about 1.5 % of them, gathered at a harbour mouth, where each decides a trip begins and ends.
  • og_cells(): the grid’s resolution, live. The page’s Cells offers, beside about a pixel at each zoom, sizes fixed at every zoom: 0.01, 0.05 (a c-square), 0.1 and 0.5 degrees and the ICES statistical rectangle (1 by 0.5 degrees), those a whole number of the cells’ own (sizes, ices, cell for the start). A size narrower than half a pixel at a zoom is drawn at a whole number of it. Served and in a bundle alike (the browser sums a rectangle from the largest level written that divides it; the c-square’s 0.05 is now written).
  • og_cells(): at least N vessels. Where the cells name their vessel (vessels, found by name), the page hides the cells of fewer than 2, 3, 5 or 10 vessels on the reader’s choice (none hidden by default: a look, not a rule), counted after the other choices, and a click shows a cell’s number of vessels.
  • og_cells() follows a time panel’s vessel (follow): Show the panel’s vessel’s effort, its gear’s (the gear of most of its hours) or the fleet’s, by setting the cells’ own vessel and gear choices as the panel’s vessel changes; hidden on a map with no panel.
  • A segment with a time follows the time panel, as a point does: a set and its haul, drawn as a segment, show the panel’s vessel and span alone.
  • A new article, “Vessel tracks”, on ramb’s public examples: trips and effort (dansk), ramb’s flags against planted faults (dansk_planted: 44 of 92 caught, 82 good pings flagged), an observer’s labels against a speed rule (ird_mg_gillnet). The site’s build installs ramb (Config/Needs/website).

ogis 2026.11.18.15

  • Values by cell as one layer function, og_cells() (the maintainer: “would like that the user could do similar thing but from within ogis”, of fishycode’s effort map; named for its format, not its first use, as other data have it). A table of cells (ix and iy, a cell’s south-west corner in steps of unit degrees; the columns chosen by; the values summed) is coloured by a value per square kilometre on ogis’s grid layer: the page has a control for each column chosen by (all, one, or several from the address; a column of years as a span; one_of, two counts of the same thing such as two definitions of fishing, one at a time) and the colours’ own. As the page asks for a tile, DuckDB sums the cells under it to about a screen pixel at that zoom, no finer than the cells’ own (read from their corners), finer or coarser by the page’s Cells. The cells: a table, a Parquet file read where it is, or nothing, the file OGIS_CELLS names (as OGIS_DEPTH). Labels and the names of codes (a gear’s id as its name) from the file’s data dictionary, else codes. The starting choices and look as arguments (filter, metric, palette, opacity, limits, stretch), the page’s address winning. og_bundle() carries it with no grids given, summed in the browser at 0.01 degrees and up.
    • On fishycode’s 0.005-degree effort grid, its fishing preset alone sorted by cell (381 MB, 32 million rows): the map built in 1.2 s; a tile at zooms 5-8 in 0.03-0.26 s (up to 5.5 MB), at zoom 10 in 0.02 s, filtered faster; finer cells up to 0.9 s and 20 MB. On its whole 0.001-degree grid (5.1 GB, both presets as one_of): built in 0.7 s, its lists in 0.9 s, a tile at zoom 6 in 1 s. Bundled with the place names in 9 s, 205 MB (the cells 192 MB, at 0.01-0.5 degrees).
  • Place names as one layer function, og_names() (the maintainer: a curated list of names, searched, clicked, “more detailed informations”; no editing). Each name from its own zoom (min_zoom), the larger first where they meet (level, then n), written beside its point where crowded; found by the page’s Find box, the map going to its zoom; a click shows the rest of its row, labelled by the file’s data dictionary. Its controls, folded: the names’ colour, and the zoom they appear at (a zoom later to two earlier), as fishycode’s names map has them. Where the names have areas, those are a layer of their own (<id>_areas), off when the page opens, a click inside one showing the same; sent whole, one file, for a few large areas (a sea’s) covered so many tiles that a bundle of them as tiles took minutes (13,330 tiles to zoom 8 in 4.4 minutes). The names: a table, a (Geo)Parquet file, any file sf reads, or nothing, the file OGIS_NAMES names. Built on og_text() and og_polygon(), so a bundle carries them and their search. Fishycode’s 9,139 names (1,575 with an area) as one 1.9 MB file: built and served in a second or two, bundled in 2.8 s (13 MB).
  • The Find box takes letters no accent makes as a keyboard without them writes them: ð as d, þ as th, æ as ae, ø as o (and œ, ß, đ, ł), so hloduvik finds Hlöðuvík, where only accents were set aside.
  • A shape that is a collection is drawn as its parts. DuckDB’s ST_AsMVT() refuses a geometry collection (as sf::st_make_valid() or a union leaves some), and a tile holding one was refused whole (HTTP 500), its other features with it. Every layer function now takes a collection’s parts of the highest dimension (ST_CollectionExtract()).
  • A grid’s first view from R (start in its config): the page opens on the choices and colours its layer gives, the address winning, as it already did for a dem layer’s. og_cells() sets it.

ogis 2026.11.18.14

  • The sea floor as two layer functions (plan 072’s step 3, at the maintainer’s word: “can we not just have a ogis wrapper”). og_relief() draws a depth model’s depth in colour and its relief shaded, as two layers; og_contour() its lines of equal depth, the charts’ depths (major, by default 10, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, 500, 1,000 m and on) a little heavier and labelled, thinner lines between them spaced by depth and zoom (minor), as the names map of Icelandic waters drew them. og_map() |> og_relief() |> og_contour() replaces some twenty lines of og_layer()s.
    • The depth model (tiles): nothing, the one OGIS_DEPTH names; an MBTiles file; a grid (a GeoTIFF, a terra raster, a data frame of cells), made into tiles by og_tiles_dem(); or a tile function. Given first, it starts a map that opens on its extent.
    • The starting look as plain arguments: palette (by default "grey", at 75 % opacity, quiet under the map’s own data, as the maintainer set the names map’s), limits (fitted to the view by default), scale, shade (TRUE, an intensity, or FALSE); major, minor, labels and colour for the lines.
    • A major depth shows from the zoom whose shallowest spacing it is at least; the lines are made at the common divisor of the spacings and the depths shown (with 25 m among them, every 5 m from zoom 7). On the Olex grid in headless Chrome a view settled in 2.6 s at zooms 7, 8 and 10, labels at 10-200 m. A label may bend as sharply as the line: at 30 or 90 degrees no label was placed on that grid’s stepped lines at zoom 10.
  • No wall of contours along a grid’s edge. Elevation tiles hold 0 (sea level) beyond a grid and on land, so every depth between a grid’s edge in open water and 0 was drawn along the edge (a box of 5-25 m lines round the Danish example’s North Sea; on the Olex grid, whose edges lie at 1,000-3,000 m, a band of hundreds). A contour layer now hands maplibre-contour a value at the fit’s nodata (0 by default) as missing, and it draws no line through a missing value; lines no longer stack along the coast either. The colours and the shading are as they were (the shading still marks the edge with a thin seam: MapLibre’s hillshade has no missing values). This needs the lines made on the page’s own thread when served, as a bundle already made them; on the Olex grid a view settled as fast. The test fails without it (12 lines along a flat grid’s edge, against none).
  • A layer’s controls can open folded (the maintainer: the depth layer’s details not shown until the reader expands it). A layer whose config has fold (as og_relief()‘s and og_contour()’s have, unless open = TRUE) shows ▸ beside its name, a click showing its controls; its colours’ scale bar and a legend show either way.
  • og_tiles_mbtiles() with no file reads the file named by the environment variable OGIS_DEPTH, a line in .Renviron (OGIS_DEPTH=D:/data/depth.mbtiles), and says so once a session; a file given wins. A depth model shared between colleagues as one MBTiles file, each keeping it where they like, is then named once on each computer and in no script. Errors say what to do: with neither, how to set the variable; with a path that is no file, or no MBTiles (SQLite) file, which path and from where, a grid pointed to og_tiles_dem(). ~ in a path is expanded. At the maintainer’s word (“Yes, build it”), from the side study of the Icelandic depth model in ogis.
  • RSQLite is imported, no longer suggested: og_tiles_mbtiles() works as soon as ogis is installed. DuckDB’s own SQLite reader was measured and set aside: it scans the whole tiles table for each tile (110 ms a tile on a 547 MB file, against RSQLite’s 0.2-0.7 ms), as it uses no index of the file.

ogis 2026.11.18.13

  • og_text(endzoom = ): where a label stops, a number (the styles’ own maxzoom) or a column written bare, each row until its own, hidden from the first whole zoom at or above it (MapLibre judges a zoom in a filter at whole zooms, as for minzoom); a row with no end shows on. With minzoom a label shows in a band of zooms, as the names editor shows its names, and two layers can take turns. A search takes the map to a zoom where its label shows, before its end. Reported by the names session (plan 076 step 6). The Labels article shows it.
  • A layer function’s minzoom as a number now holds for a layer sent whole: its styles take it. It reached the page as the layer’s own minzoom, which only a tiled layer’s source uses, so og_point(minzoom = 8) or og_text(minzoom = 10) on a layer small enough to go whole drew at every zoom. Found writing the Labels article’s example of two label layers taking turns.

ogis 2026.11.18.12

  • The engine’s guard against MapLibre 5’s lost index is gone. In 5.x a tile loaded again while an earlier load of it was still being read lost its index, and every query of that layer then threw “Out of bounds” until its data were sent again; the page caught that, sent the data again and tried a click once more. MapLibre fixed it in 6.0 and 6.3, and the reproduction that found it (data sent during an animated zoom, a filter reading the zoom from MapLibre’s global state) failed 9 times in 200 on 5.24.1 and not once in 200 on 6.19.0. Queries go straight to MapLibre; query() stays as the one place that leaves out layers not on the map.

ogis 2026.11.18.11

  • MapLibre GL JS 6.19.0 in place of 5.24.1, the last of 5.x. MapLibre 6 is published only as ES modules, which a page opened from its folder cannot load, and a bundle opens by a double click; so its two modules are made classic scripts by tools/vendor-maplibre.R (the npm package checked against the registry’s SHA-512; import.meta.url the script’s own address, the export list the global maplibregl), its worker’s code carried in maplibre-gl-worker.js and handed to MapLibre as a blob, which MapLibre 6.17 and later runs on a page opened from a file. The page loads that script before MapLibre; nothing else in it changed. A bundle is 0.6 MB larger.
  • A test opens a bundle from its folder (file://), as a double click does, and checks its outlines, labels and contours (made in the page by maplibre-contour) are drawn; every other page test opens its page over http. tools/firefox-check.R does the same in headless Firefox, by hand at each MapLibre update.
  • Checked beside 5.24.1 at the same views: lines that cross, labels past their tiles’ deepest zoom and contours look the same; a map of 8,918 labels opens and zooms as fast. The engine’s guard on queries for MapLibre 5’s lost index stays until a reproduction shows 6 has done with it.

ogis 2026.11.18.10

  • rebelrebel is renamed ogis, its prefix rr_ now og_: every function (og_map(), og_point(), og_serve(), …) and class (og_map, og_layer, og_section), and in the page what a script of its own sees: the object it is given (og: og.on(), og.state(), og.fetch(), …), the features’ key (og_row) and the classes its styles may name (.og-panel). A map’s own route header is X-OG-Notes. Names the engine kept from ramb (rb) are og too. Nothing else changed: a call made with the rr_ names is the same call with og_. The entries below keep the names of their day.
